execution_steps: 1. Ran a standalone AST scan (socket/urllib/http/ftplib/smtplib/subprocess/importlib/pkgutil/ctypes, the same forbidden-module set nrrd/xliff/ubl already use) across ipynb's full source tree: found subprocess (adapters/execute.py), urllib (model/attachments.py, validation/rules.py), importlib (validation/schema.py). Zero hits for socket/http/ftplib/smtplib/pkgutil/ctypes.

2. Investigated each ipynb hit individually before writing any assertion: subprocess is confined to adapters/execute.py (IPYNB-EXEC-001's own required opt-in, isolated execution adapter, already audit-hook-tested); both urllib hits are `from urllib.parse import quote, unquote` (pure string encoding, no network I/O -- urllib.request/urllib.error never imported); the importlib hit is `from importlib import resources` (static bundled-schema-file reading, not dynamic module loading -- confirmed no importlib.import_module or __import__ call exists anywhere in ipynb).

3. Ran the same scan across safetensors' full source tree: found importlib.import_module in adapters/numpy.py and adapters/torch.py only. Zero hits for every other forbidden module including subprocess/urllib/socket.

4. Investigated both safetensors hits: each calls importlib.import_module with a fixed string literal ("numpy", "torch") -- confirmed by reading the exact call sites -- the standard idiomatic lazy-optional-dependency pattern (the base package works with neither installed; array/tensor interop lazily imports only when a caller actually requests it), not an attacker-influenced dynamic import.

5. Added tests/python/ipynb/test_obligation_security_baseline.py (5 tests): fully-forbidden modules never imported; subprocess confined to adapters/execute.py; urllib confined to the parse submodule (urllib.request/error never imported, checked both `from urllib import request` and `import urllib.request` import forms); no dynamic importlib.import_module/__import__ call anywhere; no eval/exec/compile call anywhere (a static complement to the existing runtime audit-hook proof in test_obligation_core_path_no_execution.py).

6. Added tests/python/safetensors/test_obligation_security_baseline.py (4 tests, safetensors' first security test file of any kind): fully-forbidden modules never imported; no eval/exec/compile call anywhere; dynamic import confined to exactly the 2 known sites, each verified to pass only its own expected fixed string literal (an import_module call with any other argument, or from any other file, fails the check); a staleness guard confirming both allow-listed files still exist (so the check cannot pass vacuously after a rename).
